newsitem.title: UK: Crude moving by sea falls in week to Mar 9-analyst.
newsitem.headline: Crude moving by sea falls in week to Mar 9-analyst.

text.p: Crude oil in transit at sea globally fell to an estimated 422 million barrels in the week to March 9 from 437 million barrels the previous week, analyst Oil Movements said.
However, a fall in arrivals from now on could soon lead to a build in stocks on the water, the weekly publication said.
Oil in transit hit a two year high of 459 million barrels in the weeks ending on February 16 and February 2. It fell to an estimated 431 million barrels in the week ending on Feburary 23.
"Recent movements have been dictated by the course of outflows (arrivals) but this phase may be over," Oil Movements said.
"Global arrivals have turned down this month, and unless sailings do the same, stocks at sea could well start building again soon."
Global arrivals fell to 30.8 million barrels per day (bpd) in the week to March 8 from 33.1 million the previous week.

Sailings from OPEC members rose to 22.7 million bpd in the week to March 1 (rpt 1) from 19.2 million the previous week. Sailings from non-OPEC rose to 10.1 million bpd in the week to March 1 from 9.7 million bpd.
